node.label: State finances
node.summary: Revenue, committed spending, subsidies and accounting standards in States.

facts.text: He suggests State accounts follow the IMF's **GFSM 2014**. Counting contract staff and aided bodies lifts salary spending from 2.5% to about 4.1% of GDP; hidden subsidies need disclosure.
facts.plain: He suggests State accounts follow the IMF's GFSM 2014. Counting contract staff and aided bodies lifts salary spending from 2.5% to about 4.1% of GDP; hidden subsidies need disclosure.

facts.text: T.N.'s committed spending was about **two-thirds** of revenue receipts (2024-25), interest about one-quarter (2025-26), and capex under **1.5% of GSDP**.
facts.plain: T.N.'s committed spending was about two-thirds of revenue receipts (2024-25), interest about one-quarter (2025-26), and capex under 1.5% of GSDP.

facts.text: Tamil Nadu set up a committee on welfare and public spending. Op-ed author **Anoop Singh** was a Member of the **15th Finance Commission**.
facts.plain: Tamil Nadu set up a committee on welfare and public spending. Op-ed author Anoop Singh was a Member of the 15th Finance Commission.

facts.text: The **41%** share was set by the **15th Finance Commission** (chair **N.K. Singh**); the **16th Finance Commission** is chaired by **Arvind Panagariya**. Finance Commissions are set up under **Article 280**.
facts.plain: The 41% share was set by the 15th Finance Commission (chair N.K. Singh); the 16th Finance Commission is chaired by Arvind Panagariya. Finance Commissions are set up under Article 280.

facts.text: The Centre released an **additional tax devolution** instalment of over **₹1.09 lakh crore** to States (the second extra instalment this year) for festive-season capex. States get **41%** of divisible taxes, released in **14 instalments** a year.
